title: Lanssac to Charles IX, Warsaw, 26 April 1573, BnF fr. 4735 no. 51 f. 124, and the sibling election letters ff. 160, 164, 174

steps.what: Tomokiyo's table and Noailles 1867 checked; the 26 April letter is in neither, Tomokiyo gives no reading.
Fetched the Gallica IIIF microfilm scans of ff. 121-164 with back-off.
Transcribed 741 tokens from f. 124, f. 154, f. 154v l. 1 and f. 156.
Glossed sibling f. 154v l. 1 'car je n'ay pas cinquante' fixed 12 signs and showed Tomokiyo's row shifted.
Passage 2 of f. 124 read by hand against its gloss 'pour le moins esté retenu'.
Pinned 5-gram annealer over the whole transcription filled the free signs.
Shuffled-token and blind runs: shuffled score far worse; blind run finds a better-scoring wrong key (6 of 21 crib letters).
Lattice beam decode of both f. 124 passages; 96 of 100 signs read.
Key carried to ff. 160, 164, 174; read in substance, short runs open.
Readings agree with the surviving gloss fragments on every leaf.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the contemporary marginal decipherments beside the cipher on f. 124 and its sibling f. 154v in the same volume (BnF fr. 4735), cut by the gutter on the microfilm, with a pinned annealer filling the rest; Tomokiyo's published table was checked and found shifted.
outcome.notes: f. 124: 96 of 100 signs; siblings read in substance with four unread runs on f. 164.

prior.where: Contemporary marginal decipherment, cut by the gutter on the microfilm; Tomokiyo's table (cryptiana henryiii.htm) with no reading of any letter

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
